title: Paper 2 style practice: GreenGrain plc
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 40 (Pupil PDF worksheet: GreenGrain plc case and 20-mark Paper 2 style question (answer key in the plan))
intro: Read the case. Answer every part; use figures from the case.

passage.title: GreenGrain plc
paras: GreenGrain plc makes oat drinks and breakfast cereals in two UK factories and employs 1,800 staff. Its shares are traded on the stock exchange. It buys $2.4 million of oats a year from farms in Canada, paid in US dollars, and sells 35% of its products to the European Union.

This year the pound strengthened from £1 = $1.20 to £1 = $1.50. Labour turnover in its factories is 18% a year, against 9% for similar firms; exit interviews mention repetitive work and little chance of promotion.
The board is considering moving one factory to the EU to be closer to its European customers.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

questions.q: (a) Identify one stakeholder of GreenGrain plc.
questions.a: For example: shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers, the government (B1)

questions.q: (b) Outline one benefit to GreenGrain of being a public limited company.
questions.a: It can raise large sums by selling shares to the public (point), e.g. to fund a new factory (development)

questions.q: (c) Calculate the change in GreenGrain's annual cost of oats, in pounds, when the rate moves from £1 = $1.20 to £1 = $1.50.
(d) Analyse the effects of high labour turnover on GreenGrain.
questions.a: 18% turnover (double similar firms) means high recruitment and training costs, lost output while new staff learn, and lower quality, so costs rise and profit falls; it also damages morale. Level 3 (5-6): a balanced analysis with two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development.

questions.q: (e) Evaluate whether GreenGrain should move one factory to the EU.
questions.a: For: closer to the 35% of sales in the EU, lower transport costs, avoids any trade barriers. Against: closure costs, redundancies in the UK, recruiting abroad, and the strong pound now makes imports cheaper but EU-made goods are costed in euros. Judgement: depends on EU sales growth and trade rules. Level 4 (10-12): developed chains of reasoning on both sides in context, and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified.
